title: Protocol for immunofluorescence staining of murine helminth-infected intestinal and lung tissues
protocol: Euthanize the mouse according to approved euthanasia procedures and immediately proceed with the protocol.
Dissect the small intestine from the mouse.
Cut the small intestine at its proximal end about 1 cm from the stomach, then cut it again at the distal end, 1 cm from the cecum.
Place the dissected small intestine in a petri dish on ice filled with ice-cold 1× PBS.
Flush the small intestine slowly using an 18G feeding needle attached to a 10 ml syringe filled with ice-cold 1× PBS to remove fecal matter.
Transfer the flushed small intestine onto Whatman paper and use forceps to gently remove any excess tissue or fat.
Stretch the cleaned small intestine into an S shape and cut it into three equal segments.
Cut the segment of interest longitudinally along the length of the fragment at the mesenteric line.
Gently blot excess PBS from the luminal side using Whatman paper and a Kim wipe.
Wrap the proximal end of the small intestine around a toothpick.
Gently roll the intestine to form a Swiss-roll with curved forceps.
Submerge the rolled small intestine into the cryo-mold containing O.C.T. compound until the toothpick touches the mold’s bottom.
Slowly remove the tissue by pulling it up while holding down the tissue with surgical forceps.
Cover the rest of the tissue with O.C.T., avoiding bubbles around the tissue.
Gently pop any bubbles that occur with a toothpick.
Hold the cryo-mold containing O.C.T. and rolled tissue using large tongs/forceps.
Gently immerse three-quarters of the cryo-mold into a container with cold isopentane.
Wait for 30-60 seconds to ensure the sample freezes completely.
Avoid dropping or fully submerging the samples in isopentane, as it should not touch the O.C.T. compound.
Ensure the tissue is fully frozen without cracking.
Store the frozen tissue immediately in a foam container with dry ice until all experiment samples are frozen.
Wrap each frozen cryo-mold with square pieces of aluminum foil.
Seal wrapped cryo-molds in zipper storage bags, removing any air inside.
Place sealed and bagged samples in a cryogenic box at -80°C for long-term storage.
Set cryostat temperature between -20°C and -25°C.
Place samples for sectioning at -20°C freezer or inside the cryostat cooling chamber for 20–30 minutes.
Mount tissue onto the cryostat specimen holder (chuck) using a drop of O.C.T. medium.
Freeze tissue using the Peltier option in the cooling chamber.
Section SI tissue (4-10 μm thickness) onto Superfrost™ Plus charged slides.
Immediately after sectioning, place the slides in a Coplin jar containing -20°C cold histological grade acetone (≥99.5%).
Fix and permeabilize for 7 min.
Air dry slides for 30 min in a fume hood.
Rehydrate slides in a Coplin jar filled with 1× PBS for 10 min.
Aspirate any PBS surrounding the tissue and place it in a moist chamber box.
Immediately add the blocking buffer mixture to the slides.
Block for 1 h at (20°C and 25°C).
Wash off the blocking buffer with 1× PBS for 5 min each by placing the slides in Coplin jars.
Repeat washing step 3 times.
Aspirate any PBS surrounding the tissue and immediately add a pre-conjugated antibody to the slides.
Store the slides at 4°C in the dark overnight (∼12–16 h).
Wash slides with 1× PBS for 5–10 min each by placing the slides in Coplin jars on days 2–4.
Repeat washing step 3 times.
Stain the slides with nuclear stain Hoechst 33422 (10 μg/mL) for 30 min at (20°C and 25°C) in the dark.
Wash slides with 1× PBS for 5 min each by placing the slides in Coplin jars.
Repeat washing step 3 times.
Aspirate any PBS surrounding the tissue.
Add a drop of Prolong gold mounting media to the slides.
Slowly mount with a cover slip.
Wipe any excess mounting media from the corners using a Kim wipe.
Allow slides to harden/cure in the dark for 24–48 hours before visualizing on a microscope.
Place the slide on the stage.
Set up the imaging parameters on the software.
Start with a 10× dry objective in the suitable filter set for nuclear staining.
Focus using the z control on the microscope.
Once an area of interest is found, switch to a 20× objective.
Focus and acquire an image.
Deeply sedate mice using Ketamine (80 mg/kg)/Xylazine (10 mg/mL) via the intraperitoneal route.
Place the mouse in the ventral position.
Make an incision along the ventral midline from the groin to the chin over the sternum skin.
Grasp the peritoneal wall with forceps and make an incision to expose the gastrointestinal tract and chest cavity.
Euthanize mice through induced bleeding by cutting into the abdominal aorta.
Flip the small and large intestines to the right side using forceps.
Cut into the abdominal aorta to induce bleeding.
Make an incision through the ventral diaphragm and cut the rib cage along the sternum to expose the lungs, trachea, heart, and esophagus.
Carefully cut and remove the heart and esophagus.
Dissect the lung lobe of interest, or keep the whole pulmonary organ, trachea, and lung intact.
Immerse each tissue individually immediately in 10 mL of fresh 1% PFA in 15 mL conical tubes.
Place on a nutator, rocking gently at 4°C.
Incubate overnight (∼12–16 h).
Place lung tissues in 6-well plates filled with 1× PBS and place on a nutator, gently washing for 5 min.
Place lung tissues in 6-well plates filled with 50 mM ammonium chloride (NH4Cl) and place on a nutator, gently washing for 5 min to quench free aldehydes.
Repeat the washing step with NH4Cl three times.
Place lung tissues in 6-well plates filled with 1× PBS and place on a nutator, gently washing for 5 min.
Cryoprotect lungs by placing them in 30% (w/v) sucrose in a 15 mL conical vial and place on a nutator, rocking gently at 4°C until the tissue sinks overnight (∼12–16 h).
Place tissues on Whatman paper and gently blot to dry with a Kim wipe.
Place 1/3 O.C.T. filled cryo-mold on dry ice.
Set cryostat temperature between -20°C.
Place samples for sectioning at −20°C or inside the cryostat cooling chamber for 20–30 minutes to reach equilibrium temperature.
Mount tissue onto the cryostat specimen holder chuck.
Add a drop of O.C.T. on the chuck and adhere the tissue via the drop.
Freeze using the Peltier option in the cooling chamber.
Section lung tissue at 4–10 μm thickness onto Superfrost™ Plus charged slides.
Air dry slides for 30 minutes in a fume hood.
Rehydrate slides in a Coplin jar filled with 1× PBS for 10 minutes.
Aspirate any PBS surrounding the tissue and place slides in a moist chamber box.
Immediately add blocking buffer mixture to the slides.
Block slides for 1 hour at room temperature (20°C–25°C).
Wash off blocking buffer with 1× PBS for 5 minutes each by placing the slides in Coplin jars.
Repeat washing steps three times.
Aspirate any remaining PBS surrounding the tissue.
Immediately add pre-conjugated antibody mixture to the slides.
Store slides at 4°C in the dark overnight (∼12–16 hours).
Wash slides with 1× PBS for 5–10 minutes each by placing them in Coplin jars on days 2–4.
Repeat the staining process three times.
Stain samples with nuclear stain Hoechst 3342 (10 μg/mL) for 30 minutes in the dark.
Wash slides with 1× PBS for 5 minutes each, repeating this step three times.
Aspirate any remaining PBS from around the tissue.
Add a drop of Prolong gold mounting media to the slide.
Slowly place a cover slip over the sample.
Remove excess mounting medium from the edges of the slide.
Allow slides to cure in the dark for 24-48 hours before imaging.
Place the specimen on the microscope stage.
Set up imaging parameters using microscopy software.
Focus on an area of interest using a 10× dry objective and suitable filter set for nuclear staining.
Switch to a 20× objective, focusing again if necessary.
Acquire images with DIC lighting.
